entries.english: Dr. J. L. Krapf's (1850, Preface pp. iv, vii–viii & pp. 1–64) Kipokómo Corpus from Hadji Omar of Kalindi & Mángea Origin Traditions
entries.translation: Historical Context (Preface pp. vii–viii): Recorded in 1845 at Takaóngo (near Kilifi Bay) from Hadji Omar, brother of Bonnaia Dadia, chief of Kalindi (first Pokomo village on the Dana / Pokómo / Máro / Quilimancy river), who served as interpreter with the Galla chieftain of Berraráta; preserves the oral traditions that the Wasegéju near Tanga were originally Wapokómo expelled by the Galla, that the Wateita of Kadiáro, Ndara, and Bura call the Wanika Ambakómo from their former residence in Pokomo territory, and that the Kiriama (Giriama) lived at Mángea on the Pokomóni • Distinctive Kipokómo Governance, Kinship & Cushitic-Sabaki Lexicon (pp. 1–64): hátju / heiu (king/chief; heiyóma = kingdom; murra ja hatju = vice-regent; gása ya jiháko / gassa ya heiu = chief's council seat), manguddo (judge; yákăma = judgement, yakámisa = judge), kallu (soothsaying, p. 47), arára & nágea (peace/reconciliation; muntu ararsania = peacemaker, p. 33), zahuáje (grandfather), tjáuje (grandmother/mistress), mmétje (uncle), úmbu (sister), gáltama muke (virgin), múráni (young son/warrior), bámu (friend), óla (neighbour), mágu (news/information), sári (name), mótjo (heart/mind/soul), muázi (blood), gégo pl. magégo (tooth), zuátjo pl. niátjo (footprint/sole), zána (river), rokánga / ukánga (sea/ocean), dau & mzéfe (ship/mtepe), kibéria (axe), kéra (iron), harre (donkey), férada (horse), sánga (bull), korma (ox), nadóde (leopard), maiónda (monkey), kitungúe (hare), ungúu jua zána (hippo), uissoa (flour), kilizuío (breakfast), jakúja ja mskáhi (dinner), jakúja ja zióni (supper), huáa & hikísa (accept/take), zákka (love/want), látja (search/seek), hasáua (converse)
entries.pronunciation: ka-lin-di • bon-na-ia da-dia • ha-dji o-mar • man-ge-a • am-ba-ko-mo • ha-tju • man-gud-do
